thread:
emily (Design): quick design q — the error-context tooltip inside request drilldown reads like a mini-doc. thinking we remove the export action from that tooltip and surface a single 'Export trace' control in the drilldown header toolbar. whos for that?

raj (Product): +1. tooltip is overloaded. header-level export is more discoverable for end-users. but let's keep a small inline affordance (three-dot menu) inside the tooltip for 'Export view' so power users can still act without moving focus.

emily (Design): sounds good. tooltip would then be short and action-light. proposed tooltip text:

"Error context — top frames and request metadata. Click to expand stack and copy request id."

and header button: "Export trace" with a chevron to select JSON/HAR. avoid the word "snapshot."

maria (Eng): implementation note: exporting from header requires server to persist current filter/time-range as part of the export job. adds ~200ms and a small auth call; doable but we should document perf tradeoff.

liam (A11y): accessibility checklist: export button must be keyboard reachable, have an aria-label that includes the request id (e.g. "Export trace (request 89a4f2)"), and focus must return to a sensible element after closing modal. confirm modal has aria-modal and role dialog.

emily (Design): thanks. for placement — should Export sit left by Back or right near filters/time selector? my vote: right, grouped with filters for locality.

raj (Product): right grouping makes sense for discoverability. propose keyboard shortcut Shift+E to open export modal; add to command palette.

maria (Eng): Shift+E okay, will validate for conflicts. backend will default export to JSON containing trace + metadata; HAR as opt-in. we'll include a small metadata blob with error classification and relevant tags.

emily (Design): visual details — make Export a clear outline button, not primary. primary is still 'Back' in drilldown flow. also ensure icon contrast meets 4.5:1.

liam (A11y): agree on outline. Also DOM order should place Export before overflow menu for keyboard users, even if visually it's to the right. we'll add screenreader hint: "Includes filters and visible frames."

ui-bot: preview deployed at https://ui-stage.redwood.ai/trace-export-170210 — includes keyboard shortcut demo and JSON export.

raj (Product): I'll update the product copy doc to use "Export trace" + microcopy "Includes filters, time range, and visible stack frames." Can we do a short sync tomorrow 11am to sign off?

emily (Design): 11am works. I'll push updated Figma screens and tag the team.

maria (Eng): works for me.

liam (A11y): works. I'll bring a11y checklist and run the contrast scan. :thumbsup:
